messages.subject: secr 4.4.4, openCR 2.0.2
messages.body_plain:
Both secr and openCR have been updated on CRAN in the last month. openCR 2.0 has significant new capability, including stratum-level models and new 'sparse' movement kernels. Several bugs have been fixed. For details see the NEWS for secr <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/secr%204.4.4%20NEWS.txt> and openCR <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/openCR%202.0.2%20NEWS.txt>.
Murray

messages.subject: JSSAsecrD failing in openCR 2.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

I’m having an issue using the new openCR 2.0. Basically all attempts at using JSSAsecrD models are failing. openCR 1.4 worked fine and I haven’t changed my code.

Eigenvalues :  NaN NaN NaN NaN

Numerical rank of Hessian : 0  ( svtol = 1e-05 )

Warning: at least one real parameter is not identifiable

Non-spatial models JSSAN using the same dataset in openCR 2.0 are working fine, generating reasonable estimates.

Capthist summary is not revealing any errors.

Could there be an issue with my mask that I am missing?

wd = paste(getwd(), "/Pen_boundary", sep="")

library(rgdal)

fence = readOGR(dsn=wd,layer="Pen_boundary_plus20m_GDA94MGA51", verbose=FALSE)

mask.clipped = make.mask(traps=traps(BL),

                         buffer=4*185,

                         spacing=1*185,

                         poly=fence,

                         poly.habitat = TRUE)

plot(mask.clipped)

plot(traps(BL), add=TRUE)

plot(BL, add=TRUE, tracks=TRUE)

Really appreciate any help you can provide.

Thanks,

Cheryl

If you like, send an example offline, with data. I wonder also why you choose to use openCR for closed-model density estimation. when 'secr' is designed for that job.

messages.subject: Heterogeneous camera trapping data
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I work on
SCR analysis to estimate Balkan lynx density in North
Macedonia. I have four sessions of camera trapping over the same period but
with very heterogenous results:

-
2013
: 33 recaptures / 9 individuals

-
2015
: 17 recaptures / 8 individuals

-
2018
: 31 recaptures / 10 individuals

-
2021
: 8 recaptures / 4 individuals

I know I
don’t have enough individuals and/or recaptures on some years (2015, 2021) to
do a single session analysis. Moreover closure.test indicate an open area for 2013 : 3 lynx captured only once, one lynx twice but only one of them never recaptured.

My question is : does a
multi-season model allow me to use those years where there is less data? Any
idea not to “lose” those years ?

I hope the
answer is not so obvious and not just no …

Thank you
in advance !

Yon

messages.subject: Re: Heterogeneous camera trapping data
messages.body_plain:
A multisession analysis allows you to fit a model with each detection parameter (g0 or lambda0 and sigma) held at the same value across years (e.g. g0~1, sigma~1). If that is a reasonable assumption (I expect it is) then there is no reason to 'lose' any data. It's worth also checking by AIC whether there is clear evidence for annual variation in density (D~session vs D~1). The 'heterogeneity' you see may just be sampling variation (although I expect not).
Murray
